dos.text: Attach real interactive behavior at the outer toolbox container level, not per individual <toolbar>, that's how navigator-toolbox.js's own event delegation actually works.
Treat nav-bar, PersonalToolbar, and TabsToolbar as the same real pattern, events just bubble up from buttons inside them to one shared container listener.

donts.text: Don't look for a distinct "toolbar" implementation separate from "toolbox", there isn't one in this file, it's the same underlying event delegation either way.

behavior.text: A <toolbar> has no interactive implementation of its own; navigator-toolbox.js delegates all real event handling (popupshowing, command) from the outer #navigator-toolbox container, the same mechanism toolbox itself uses.

reference.text: The W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide's toolbar pattern expects roving-tabindex keyboard navigation: Tab/Shift+Tab enter and exit the whole toolbar as a single stop, and arrow keys move focus between its individual controls, reserved for grouping 3 or more controls. Not confirmed here whether Firefox's real toolbar implementation follows this exact model, only that this is the established external convention for the role.
